symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Number of adaptively randomized decision occasions.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: Decision-occasion index.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Number of treatment arms.

symbols.name: \mathcal A
symbols.def: Set of randomized treatment arms.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: Dimension of the stacked causal parameter.

symbols.name: \Theta
symbols.def: Parameter space for the stacked arm-specific marginal moment target.

symbols.name: \mathcal X
symbols.def: Context space observed before randomization.

symbols.name: X_t
symbols.def: Context observed at occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: Y_t(a)
symbols.def: Potential outcome at occasion \(t\) under arm \(a\in\mathcal A\).

symbols.name: W_t
symbols.def: Full-data vector \(W_t=(X_t,(Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A})\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Law of the sequential full-data draws and adaptive randomization.

symbols.name: A_t
symbols.def: Treatment randomized at occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: Y_t
symbols.def: Observed outcome \(Y_t=Y_t(A_t)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_t
symbols.def: Filtration generated by observations and randomizations through occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: Dimension of the adaptive policy state.

symbols.name: \mathsf H
symbols.def: State space for the adaptive recursion.

symbols.name: \eta_t
symbols.def: Policy state after occasion \(t\), measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_t\).

symbols.name: \eta_0
symbols.def: Policy state before the first adaptive randomization.

symbols.name: \Pi
symbols.def: Policy map whose arm probabilities sum to one for every context and state.

symbols.name: \pi_t
symbols.def: Logged randomization probability \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})=\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta_{t-1})\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: Uniform exploration floor.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Common envelope for the causal score over the triangular-array class.

symbols.name: D_1
symbols.def: Common envelope for the first parameter derivative of the causal score.

symbols.name: D_2
symbols.def: Common envelope for the second parameter derivative of the causal score.

symbols.name: h_-
symbols.def: Common lower singular-value bound for the population Jacobian.

symbols.name: L_\Pi
symbols.def: Common Lipschitz modulus for the policy map.

symbols.name: \omega_-
symbols.def: Common lower eigenvalue bound for every basin score covariance.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: Common separation modulus for the population causal moment away from its root.

symbols.name: s_\Theta
symbols.def: Common interior-radius bound for the causal moment root.

symbols.name: g
symbols.def: Stacked arm-specific causal estimating function evaluated at an action, context, potential outcome, and parameter.

symbols.name: M_P
symbols.def: Population causal moment \(M_P(\theta)=E_P[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)]\).

symbols.name: \theta^*
symbols.def: Distinguished marginal causal moment root satisfying \(M_P(\theta^*)=0\).

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.def: Common radius for local exact-root search, fixed so that the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\) lies inside the smoothness and interiority neighborhood and \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Prespecified contrast of the causal moment parameter.

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: Causal contrast \(\tau=c^\top\theta^*\).

symbols.name: \xi_t
symbols.def: Adaptive IPW score \(\xi_t=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}g(a,X_t,Y_t;\theta^*)/\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\).

symbols.name: S_T
symbols.def: Cumulative score \(S_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t\).

symbols.name: \langle S\rangle_T
symbols.def: Predictable quadratic variation \(\langle S\rangle_T=\sum_{t=1}^TE_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\).

symbols.name: [S]_T
symbols.def: Realized quadratic variation \([S]_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t\xi_t^\top\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Population Jacobian \(H=\partial_\theta E_P[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)]|_{\theta=\theta^*}\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of candidate deterministic tail attractors.

symbols.name: \bar\eta_j
symbols.def: Candidate attractor state indexed by \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: Tail basin selected by the adaptive recursion.

symbols.name: \mathcal J
symbols.def: Positive-mass support of the selected basin, \(\mathcal J=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:P(J=j)>0\}\).

symbols.name: \bar\eta_J
symbols.def: Selected attractor \(\bar\eta_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\bar\eta_j\).

symbols.name: p_j
symbols.def: Basin probability \(p_j=P(J=j)\).

symbols.name: \Omega_j
symbols.def: Basin score covariance obtained by replacing \(\pi_t\) with \(\Pi(\cdot\mid X_t,\bar\eta_j)\) in \(E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\).

symbols.name: \Omega_J
symbols.def: Selected-basin score covariance \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\).

symbols.name: V_j
symbols.def: Basin estimator covariance \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\).

symbols.name: V_J
symbols.def: Selected-basin covariance \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Gaussian innovation independent of \(\sigma(J)\).

symbols.name: G_T
symbols.def: Empirical IPW moment \(G_T(\theta)=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}g(a,X_t,Y_t;\theta)/\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\).

symbols.name: \widetilde\theta_T
symbols.def: Measurable preliminary approximate minimizer of the empirical IPW moment norm.

symbols.name: \mathcal Z_T
symbols.def: Local empirical-root set \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\).

symbols.name: E_T
symbols.def: Exact-root existence event \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\theta_T
symbols.def: Total measurable IPW-Z estimator obtained by selecting an exact empirical root from \(\mathcal Z_T\) on \(E_T\) and using \(\widetilde\theta_T\) on \(E_T^c\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_T
symbols.def: Contrast estimator \(\widehat\tau_T=c^\top\widehat\theta_T\).

symbols.name: \widehat H_T
symbols.def: Empirical derivative \(\widehat H_T=\partial_\theta G_T(\widehat\theta_T)\).

symbols.name: \widehat\xi_t
symbols.def: IPW score \(\xi_t\) evaluated at \(\widehat\theta_T\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Omega_T
symbols.def: Feasible realized score covariance \(\widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E_T
symbols.def: Uniform invertibility event \(\mathcal E_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2,\ \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat V_T
symbols.def: Event-truncated realized-QV sandwich \(\widehat V_T=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_T}\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}+\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_T^c}I_d\); the inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal E_T\).

symbols.name: T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)
symbols.def: Realized-QV studentized statistic for contrast \(c\).

symbols.name: \Sigma
symbols.def: Fixed sandwich matrix used by a conventional Wald report.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: Nominal noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: \Phi
symbols.def: Standard normal distribution function.

symbols.name: z_{1-\alpha/2}
symbols.def: Quantile \(z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).

symbols.name: C_T^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)
symbols.def: Two-sided Wald interval based on the deterministic sandwich \(\Sigma\).

symbols.name: r_T
symbols.def: Cesaro policy-state error tolerance at horizon \(T\).

symbols.name: \delta_T
symbols.def: Tail probability in the uniform attraction modulus at horizon \(T\).

symbols.name: e_T
symbols.def: Common triangular-array error envelope \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak P_T
symbols.def: Finite-attractor adaptive-experiment law class at horizon \(T\), indexed by fixed common constants and moduli.

symbols.name: R_{t,a}
symbols.def: Independent centered two-point innovation with \(P(R_{t,a}=+1)=P(R_{t,a}=-1)=1/2\), independent across occasions and arms and independent of the contexts.

symbols.name: \sigma_a
symbols.def: Reward-innovation scale for arm \(a\), with \(\sigma_a^2\) fixed at the variance of the corresponding Gaussian innovation in Guo and Xu, Section 3.1.

symbols.name: \Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}
symbols.def: Guo--Xu no-intercept arm-specific ridge Gram state after occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}
symbols.def: Guo--Xu no-intercept arm-specific ridge response state after occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: \widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}
symbols.def: Arm-specific no-intercept ridge slope \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\).

symbols.name: q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}
symbols.def: Inverse ridge Gram state \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=1/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\).

symbols.name: Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t
symbols.def: Sufficient state \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) for the bounded clipped-LinUCB recursion.

symbols.name: \mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Compact set \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}=[-M_{\mathrm{GX}},M_{\mathrm{GX}}]^2\times[0,1]^2\) containing every augmented-chain state from the prescribed initialization.

symbols.name: \mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Compact index set \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}=[-1,1]^2\) for the two initial slopes; it is not the state space of the augmented Markov chain.

symbols.name: \iota_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Embedding \(\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\) of an initial-slope pair into the augmented chain.

symbols.name: m_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Number of distinct deterministic projected slope limits quantified in the bounded Guo--Xu dynamics question.

symbols.name: \bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_j
symbols.def: Distinct deterministic projected slope limit indexed by \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m_{\mathrm{GX}}\}\) in the bounded Guo--Xu dynamics question.

symbols.name: P_{\eta_0}
symbols.def: Probability law of the augmented bounded-noise Guo--Xu chain started from \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)\) for \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\).

symbols.name: J_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Tail-measurable index of the attained deterministic limit of the slope projection of the augmented bounded Guo--Xu chain.

symbols.name: B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j
symbols.type: subset of the compact initial-slope index set
symbols.def: Positive-probability basin \(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j=\{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}:P_{\eta_0}(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j)>0\}\).

symbols.name: K_0
symbols.def: Compact collection of initial slopes contained in the union of basin interiors relative to \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\).

symbols.name: r_T(K_0)
symbols.def: Compact-set Cesaro attraction tolerance at horizon \(T\) in the bounded-dynamics question.

symbols.name: \delta_T(K_0)
symbols.def: Compact-set attraction failure probability at horizon \(T\) in the bounded-dynamics question.

symbols.name: \Theta_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Parameter space that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to specify separately from the dynamics question.

symbols.name: g_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Causal score that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to specify separately from the dynamics question.

symbols.name: \theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Unique causal-score root that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to define and verify.

symbols.name: c_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Nonzero contrast that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to specify.

symbols.name: \tau_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Scalar target \(\tau_{\mathrm{GX}}=c_{\mathrm{GX}}^\top\theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}\) that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to define.

symbols.name: P^{\dagger}
symbols.def: Law of the explicit bounded two-basin adaptive experiment in the directional--matrix separation construction.

assumptions.condition: The vectors \(W_1,\ldots,W_T\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
Conditional on \(X_t\) and \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the action \(A_t\) is drawn from the logged distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\).
For every \(t\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), context, and realized history, \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\ge\varepsilon\).
The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.
constants: \(B<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.
constants: \(D_1,D_2<\infty\) and \(\rho>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(\kappa(u)>0\) for every \(u>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

standard.name: Uniform separation of a Z-functional root

constants: \(s_\Theta>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(h_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The common policy modulus satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,x\in\mathcal X}|\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)-\Pi(a\mid x,\eta')|\le L_\Pi\|\eta-\eta'\|_2\) for all \(\eta,\eta'\in\mathsf H\).
constants: \(L_\Pi<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: There is a tail variable \(J\in\mathcal J\), measurable with respect to the sigma-field generated by \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge1}\), such that \(\eta_t\to\bar\eta_J\) almost surely under \(P\).

novel.justification: Finite tail selection describes stochastic-approximation rules with several isolated locally stable equilibria, including clipped policy recursions whose early assignments select a persistent operating regime.

A Cesaro attraction modulus records the fraction of decisions made away from the selected long-run policy. It can be bounded using lock-in tails for stochastic approximation and estimated from replicated adaptive deployments.

assumptions.condition: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).

novel.justification: The combined envelope is a proposal-specific class-level restriction coupling sampling fluctuation, Cesaro attraction error, and attraction-tail probability. It is directly satisfied by immediately locking finite-state adaptive rules and can be audited from replicated policy paths; Mourrat supplies only the martingale central-limit ingredient used after this envelope is imposed.

assumptions.condition: The basin covariances satisfy \(\Omega_j\succeq\omega_-I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).
constants: \(\omega_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

novel.justification: A common lower eigenvalue bound over every positive-mass basin and every member law is a proposal-specific uniform class restriction, stronger than Saco's pointwise variance-growth condition. It is satisfied by bounded finite-policy families whose arm probabilities stay uniformly positive and whose arm-score covariance spans every target direction; the upper bound \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) follows from the bounded score and overlap conditions and is not primitive.

definitions.name: finite-attractor adaptive-experiment class
definitions.construction: For fixed \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\) and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T=\{P:\text{at horizon }T,\ P\text{ satisfies every condition in }\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\text{ with these same fixed envelopes and moduli}\}\).

definitions.name: adaptive IPW-Z estimator
definitions.construction: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).

definitions.name: bounded two-basin separation witness
definitions.construction: For every \(T\ge2\), let \(P^{\dagger}\) be the law with \(K=3\), \(d=2\), \(\Theta=[-1,1]^2\), \(\theta^*=0\), a singleton \(\mathcal X\), and constant \(X_t\). Independently across \(t\) and between arms, let \(Y_t(1)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{2/5},\sqrt{2/5}\}\), let \(Y_t(2)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{1/2},\sqrt{1/2}\}\), and set \(Y_t(3)=0\). Set \(g(1,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta_1,0)^\top\), \(g(2,x,y;\theta)=(0,y-\theta_2)^\top\), and \(g(3,x,y;\theta)=0\). Take \(m=2\), \(q=1\), \(\mathsf H=[0,1]\), \(\bar\eta_1=0\), \(\bar\eta_2=1\), and linearly interpolate the context-free policy between \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,0)=(2/5,1/4,7/20)\) and \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,1)=(2/5,1/6,13/30)\). Start at \(\eta_0=1/2\), set \(J=1\) if and only if \(A_1=1\), set \(J=2\) otherwise, and put \(\eta_t=\bar\eta_J=J-1\) for every \(t\ge1\).

definitions.name: basin-indexed covariance
definitions.construction: For each \(j\in\mathcal J\), set \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\), \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\), and \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\).

definitions.name: event-truncated realized-QV sandwich
definitions.construction: Set \(\widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top\) and \(\mathcal E_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2,\ \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\}\). Define \(\widehat V_T=\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}\) on \(\mathcal E_T\) and \(\widehat V_T=I_d\) on \(\mathcal E_T^c\).

definitions.name: basin-stable convergence criterion
definitions.construction: The convergence \(\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\to_{\mathrm{st}}-V_J^{1/2}Z\) relative to \(\sigma(J)\) means \(E_P[h(J)f(\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*))]\to E_P[h(J)f(-V_J^{1/2}Z)]\) for every bounded measurable \(h\) and bounded continuous \(f\); uniformity over \(\mathfrak P_T\) means the corresponding supremum discrepancy tends to zero for unit-bounded Lipschitz \(f\) and unit-bounded \(h\).

definitions.name: bounded-noise Guo--Xu no-intercept recursion
definitions.construction: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and each \(\sigma_a^2\) equals the variance of the corresponding Gaussian innovation in Guo and Xu, Section 3.1. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), apply a fixed tie rule to maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

definitions.name: bounded-recursion dynamics certification handle
definitions.construction: Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for a current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is \(q_a^+=q_a/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\) and \(\beta_a^+=(\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a))/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\). The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. Analyze this augmented chain on \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}\): the set is invariant because an updated slope is a convex combination of its preceding value and \(Y(a)/X\), while an unupdated slope is fixed and every inverse-Gram coordinate stays in \([0,1]\). Classify projected almost-sure limit sets directly from the augmented transition kernel; any stochastic-approximation ODE used in this classification must be derived for the augmented chain. If the projected limits are finitely many isolated deterministic states, combine compact containment in relative basin interiors with a finite-cover argument to seek the common Cesaro moduli \(r_T(K_0)\) and \(\delta_T(K_0)\).

statements.statement: For the common envelopes defining \(\mathfrak P_T\), the existing derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply the nonprimitive upper bounds \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\) and \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\). There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P[\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\|_{\mathrm{op}}]\le C(r_T+\delta_T)\). The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, and bounded-IPW martingale concentration gives \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply by a quantitative inverse-function argument that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it lies at distance \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it belongs to \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), \(G_T(\widehat\theta_T)=0\) on \(E_T\), and the fallback \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\) occurs only on a uniformly negligible event. With \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), the exact-root linearization is \(\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)\), and \((\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*),J,T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T)\) converges stably relative to \(\sigma(J)\) to \((-V_J^{1/2}Z,J,\Omega_J)\). If \(c^\top V_jc\) differs across two positive-mass basins, the unconditional limit of \(c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\) is a non-Gaussian centered normal scale mixture.
statements.justification: This theorem derives the random-QV stable limit and an explicit common \(r_T+\delta_T\) predictable-QV error while proving high-probability local exact-root existence, so the first-order Z-expansion contains no omitted estimating-equation residual.
statements.gap: Guo and Xu prove ordinary Gaussian inference under scaled inverse-propensity convergence and illustrate two policy modes numerically; they do not derive a basin-measurable stable limit from the recursion.
statements.consumer: A HeartSteps-style online learner can report the correct repeated-deployment law for a prespecified causal excursion contrast when early randomization selects among persistent policy regimes.

statements.statement: Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), \(T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\widehat H_T-H=O_P(e_T)\). Consequently \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\to0\), so the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly, \(\widehat V_T-V_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). This uniform statement strictly strengthens Saco's pointwise realized-QV pivot on the conditional finite-attractor class by deriving the variance-ratio, invertibility-event, and inverse-QV controls from the common attraction and exact-root localization controls.
statements.justification: The always-defined truncated sandwich follows the realized basin, is uniformly untruncated asymptotically, and removes the Gaussian scale mixture without estimating basin probabilities.
statements.gap: Saco proves a pointwise self-normalized martingale theorem under abstract variance growth; the unresolved step is uniform verification for an endogenous finite-attractor recursion under common attraction and exact-root localization controls.
statements.consumer: The result gives a feasible standard-normal Wald procedure for causal excursion contrasts in adaptive mobile-health experiments with path-dependent assignment regimes.

statements.statement: Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic \(\Sigma\). Under the stable limit in Theorem 1 with \(p_j>0\), \(\lim_{T\to\infty}P\{\tau\in C_T^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) if and only if \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\). The necessity is an equality-of-laws result for the finite centered Gaussian scale mixture, not a variance-matching argument at one nominal level.
statements.justification: The theorem characterizes exactly when conventional fixed-sandwich reporting remains valid for one causal contrast despite random policy regimes.
statements.gap: Directional-stability results give sufficient target-specific conditions, while Saco warns about random predictable variance; neither paper states the every-level converse for a finite basin mixture.
statements.consumer: Trial analysts can determine whether an existing deterministic variance report remains valid for one prespecified HeartSteps excursion-effect contrast even when other directions are unstable.

statements.statement: A single deterministic matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if \(V_j=\Sigma\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\). Equivalently, \(V_J\) is almost surely deterministic. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality follows by polarization.
statements.justification: This separates target-specific validity from target-agnostic covariance stability with an exact matrixwise frontier.
statements.gap: Shen and coauthors distinguish directional from target-agnostic stability on the sufficiency side; the finite-basin necessity and its equivalence to deterministic \(V_J\) remain unstated.
statements.consumer: Software that reports simultaneous Wald inference for many adaptive-experiment contrasts can use the theorem to decide when one fixed covariance matrix is defensible.

statements.statement: For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). Specifically, the policy floor is \(1/6\), \(\sup_{a,\theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2<2\), the derivative and curvature bounds are \(1\) and \(0\), \(M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=-\theta\), every empirical moment admits an exact minimum of zero in \(\Theta\), and \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2=1/(2T)\) almost surely. Moreover, \(P^{\dagger}(J=1)=2/5\), \(P^{\dagger}(J=2)=3/5\), so \(\mathcal J=\{1,2\}\); tail selection is exact after the first assignment, \(H=-I_2\), \(\Omega_1=V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), and \(\Omega_2=V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)\). Hence for \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\), \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c=1\) in both positive-mass basins although \(V_1\ne V_2\), so contrastwise deterministic-sandwich validity holds while matrixwise invariance fails.
statements.justification: This elementary bounded construction verifies inside the stated law class that the contrastwise and matrixwise frontiers are logically distinct.
statements.gap: This is a non-novel existence witness, not evidence about the Guo--Xu recursion; its role is to prevent the directional and matrix claims from being conflated by an unattained free-matrix example.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can retain a valid primary-endpoint interval in a concrete adaptive experiment without claiming that all secondary contrasts share a stable covariance.

statements.statement: For the augmented compact Markov chain \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\in\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}\) generated by the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion, with initial slopes \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}=[-1,1]^2\), initialization \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)\), and law \(P_{\eta_0}\), characterize the almost-sure limit set of the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\). In particular, determine whether there exist \(m_{\mathrm{GX}}\ge1\), distinct deterministic states \(\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_1,\ldots,\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}\in\mathbb R^2\), and a tail-measurable \(J_{\mathrm{GX}}\in\{1,\ldots,m_{\mathrm{GX}}\}\) such that \(P_{\eta_0}\{(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\to\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\}=1\) for every \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), with \(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j\) if and only if the projected limit equals \(\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_j\). If this finite family exists, identify \(m_{\mathrm{GX}}\), the projected limit states, and the initial-slope basins \(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j=\{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}:P_{\eta_0}(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j)>0\}\), and determine whether, for every compact \(K_0\subset\bigcup_{j=1}^{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}\operatorname{relint}_{\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j)\), there exist deterministic \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\to0\) satisfying \(\sup_{\eta_0\in K_0}P_{\eta_0}\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,2})^\top-\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\|_2>r_T(K_0)\}\le\delta_T(K_0)\). If finite projected tail selection fails, characterize the projected almost-sure limit set instead. Any ODE or stochastic-approximation reduction must be derived for the augmented chain and may not treat the slopes alone as Markov or \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\) as invariant. This question concerns only the bounded-analogue dynamics and asserts neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of Theorems 1--2. Any future inference result must separately define \(g_{\mathrm{GX}}\), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{GX}}\), a unique \(\theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}\), a nonzero \(c_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and \(\tau_{\mathrm{GX}}=c_{\mathrm{GX}}^\top\theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and must verify every class assumption.
statements.justification: This dynamics-only question isolates the unverified premise behind the numerical two-mode example: finite almost-sure selection of projected slope limits and relative-basin-interior Cesaro attraction for a fully specified augmented bounded recursion.
statements.gap: Borkar gives local lock-in conditional on entry into an attraction domain, Pemantle gives unstable-point avoidance, and Guo--Xu Section 3.1 gives a Gaussian-noise simulation; none classifies the projected almost-sure limit set of the augmented chain or proves finite projected tail selection with relative-basin-interior uniform attraction for this bounded Rademacher analogue.
statements.consumer: A solution would determine the bounded analogue's operating regimes and state exactly what additional, separately specified causal-score verification would be required before any inference theorem could be invoked.

statements.statement:
Let \(p\in[1,\infty)\), \(\gamma>0\), and let \((X_i,\mathcal G_i)_{i=1}^n\) be a scalar martingale-difference sequence with \(n\ge2\) and \(\max_i\|X_i\|_\infty\le\gamma\). Put \(s^2=\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2]\), \(V^2=s^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2\mid\mathcal G_{i-1}]\), and \(D=\sup_x|P\{s^{-1}\sum_iX_i\le x\}-\Phi(x)|\). There is a constant \(C_{p,\gamma}\) such that
\[
D\le C_{p,\gamma}\left\{\frac{n\log n}{s^3}+\left(\|V^2-1\|_p^p+s^{-2p}\right)^{1/(2p+1)}\right\}.
\]

attestation.note: Checked directly against the source-of-record arXiv HTML for Theorem 1.4 and equation (1.5).

statements.statement:
Let \((X_{n,t},\mathcal G_{n,t})_{t=1}^{k_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference array, \(S_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}\), \(Q_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}^2\), and \(A_n^2=\sum_tE[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}]\). If \(A_n^2\to\infty\) in probability, \(P(Q_n>0)\to1\), \(Q_n/A_n^2\to1\) in probability, and for some \(\delta>0\),
\[
 A_n^{-(2+\delta)}\sum_tE[|X_{n,t}|^{2+\delta}]\to0,
\]
then \(S_n/\sqrt{Q_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).

upstream.citation: Hall and Heyde, Martingale Limit Theory and Its Application (1980)

attestation.note: Checked directly against the source-of-record arXiv HTML for Theorem A.1; the source itself identifies Hall--Heyde Theorem 3.10 as upstream.

statements.statement: For Saco's logged-propensity, predictably scored martingale AIPW/DML estimator at a prespecified horizon, the realized-quadratic-variation score statistic and its feasible Studentized version converge pointwise to \(N(0,1)\), and the associated Wald interval has asymptotically correct coverage without a deterministic variance-stabilization assumption.

attestation.note: Checked directly against the source-of-record arXiv HTML for Theorem 5.14 and its coverage conclusion.

sampling_model.design: Known, logged, context-dependent randomization \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})=\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta_{t-1})\) updated by a history-measurable recursion.
sampling_model.units: A growing sequence of independent full-data decision occasions \(W_t\); the inferential dependence is induced by the common adaptive policy state.
sampling_model.treatment: A finite action set with sequential randomization and consistency \(Y_t=Y_t(A_t)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Known clipping floor \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\ge\varepsilon\), common over the triangular-array law class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No outcome-model nuisance is required for identification; a preliminary moment-norm minimizer localizes a total measurable exact-root selector, the Z-Jacobian and realized score quadratic variation are estimated on the observed adaptive path, and the sandwich is set to \(I_d\) off the common invertibility event.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A realized-quadratic-variation studentized martingale score is pointwise asymptotically standard normal without deterministic variance stabilization under abstract moment and variance-growth conditions.
Scaled inverse-propensity convergence yields ordinary Gaussian IPW-Z inference with a consistent sandwich estimator.
Directional stability suffices for target-specific efficient normal inference and is weaker than target-agnostic matrix stability.

For generalized Gaussian Thompson sampling, the joint optimal-arm pull-proportion and noise limit is the unique invariant law of a continuous-state SDE; normalized means are Gaussian for stable arms and have an SDE-defined semi-universal limit for multiple optimal arms, whose quantiles yield confidence intervals.

Off-policy M-estimation under working-model misspecification targets a projected solution under a stationary evaluation policy and uses flexible variance stabilization to permit unstable or nonconvergent adaptive logging policies.
Conditional on entering an attraction domain, stochastic approximation locks into a prescribed stable equilibrium with an explicit high-probability bound.

tldr: The field-tier contribution is a conditional finite-attractor theorem bundle for adaptive causal IPW-Z inference. Under common score, derivative, Jacobian-lower-bound, policy, covariance-lower-bound, root-separation, attraction, and local root-search envelopes, with attainable basins defined as the positive-mass support of the tail selector, the bundle derives a basin-stable finite Gaussian mixture with predictable-QV error controlled by \(r_T+\delta_T\), proves that an always-defined same-path realized-QV sandwich is uniformly pivotal and asymptotically untruncated, and gives exact deterministic-sandwich boundaries: every-level validity for one contrast holds if and only if that contrast's variance is basin-invariant, while validity for all contrasts holds if and only if the full covariance is deterministic. Theorem 2 has one direct strict-tightening comparator, Saco's pointwise realized-QV result; the remaining named papers provide motivation, ingredients, or orthogonal regimes rather than a second strict frontier. An elementary bounded two-basin law verifies that contrastwise invariance need not imply matrix invariance. The slope-projected limit set of the augmented bounded Guo--Xu Markov chain remains an open dynamics question with no class-membership or inference claim.

project_justification.gap: Saco supplies the one direct pointwise realized-QV comparator, but not uniform verification over an endogenous finite-attractor class. Guo--Xu and Shen and coauthors supply adjacent stable-policy and directional-stability results, Han studies continuous SDE-invariant Thompson-sampling pull proportions and raw-arm-mean inference, and Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas study stationary-evaluation-policy off-policy M-estimation with flexible variance stabilization under unstable logging. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy instead study pooled longitudinal adaptive sampling with Z-estimation and an adaptive sandwich estimator in a fixed-within-user, growing-participant regime. Existing stochastic-approximation results control lock-in only after entry into an attraction domain, and the Guo--Xu two-mode example remains numerical.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied field-tier object is a conditional recursion-level uniform limit theory that preserves the random basin, validates a finite-sample-defined same-path studentizer, and states exact contrastwise and matrixwise boundaries for deterministic-sandwich inference. The absence of a second direct strict-tightening comparator caps the positioning at field tier, which is the requested floor and achieved target.
project_justification.fill: The publishable contribution is the conditional finite-attractor theorem bundle: a basin-stable causal IPW-Z finite Gaussian mixture, a uniformly feasible same-path realized-QV pivot, and exact contrastwise and matrixwise deterministic-sandwich boundaries. A finite-attractor class indexed by common score, derivative, Jacobian lower, policy, covariance lower, root-separation, attraction, and local root-search envelopes converts policy dynamics into predictable-QV control with error \(r_T+\delta_T\); its attainable-basin index set is the positive-mass support of the tail selector. The score and derivative envelopes already imply \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) and \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\), so no primitive upper matrix bounds are imposed. The proposal-specific envelope \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\) combines sampling, attraction, and approximation errors. A preliminary moment-norm minimizer localizes a compact empirical-root set; martingale concentration and a quantitative inverse-function argument make the exact-root selector active with probability tending uniformly to one. Stable martingale convergence supplies the mixture, event-truncated realized QV supplies the feasible pivot, finite normal-mixture identification plus polarization supplies the two necessity results, and a bounded in-class law certifies strict logical separation of the directional and matrix frontiers.

related_work: Guo and Xu, Theorems 3.2--3.3, prove marginal and joint IPW-Z Gaussian limits after scaled inverse propensities stabilize; their Section 3.1 no-intercept clipped-LinUCB example supplies numerical evidence of two modes, not a proved finite-attractor theorem or certification of the present class. Guo--Xu is an informed-by comparator. Saco, Theorem 5.14 and Design A in Section 6.6, establishes a pointwise realized-QV pivot under variance growth and illustrates random post-burn-in variance; Theorem 2 is the sole direct strict tightening, giving uniform validity over the conditional finite-attractor class and deriving truncation inactivity from common basin-covariance, attraction, and exact-root localization controls. The Abstract and Introduction of Shen and coauthors distinguish directional stability from full-matrix stability; that distinction informs Theorems 3--4, while the finite-basin every-level converses and bounded separation witness are not presented as a strict comparator chain. Han studies an orthogonal instability mechanism and target: for generalized Gaussian Thompson sampling, Proposition 2.6 and Theorem 2.7 on PDF pages 9--10, together with introduction equation (1.4) on page 4, identify the joint optimal-arm pull-proportion and noise limit with the unique invariant law of a continuous-state SDE. Han's Theorem 3.2 on PDF page 12 and introduction equation (1.5) on page 5 give Gaussian normalized-mean limits for stable arms and an SDE-defined semi-universal limit for multiple optimal arms; the body reports simulation evidence that the latter law is genuinely non-Gaussian, and Corollary 3.3 on PDF page 13 constructs confidence intervals from its quantiles. Han is close motivation, not a result anticipating Theorems 1--4 or the bounded Guo--Xu certification question. Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas study off-policy M-estimation under working-model misspecification for adaptively collected bandit data. Their target is a projected solution under a stationary evaluation policy, and flexible variance stabilization permits unstable or nonconvergent logging policies; this is an informed-by comparator rather than a same-path-QV or finite-attractor result. Borkar supplies local lock-in bounds, and Pemantle supplies unstable-point avoidance, but neither certifies the bounded recursion. Aldous and Eagleson supply stable-convergence language. Mourrat supplies only the bounded-martingale central-limit and quadratic-variation ingredient. Teicher together with Andrews and Mallows supplies identification of centered normal scale mixtures. Qian and coauthors and Liao and coauthors define the HeartSteps causal-excursion consumer. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy study pooled longitudinal adaptive sampling with Z-estimation and an adaptive sandwich estimator in a fixed-within-user, growing-participant regime. Thus the comparison supports a field-tier conditional theorem bundle, with Saco as its only strict-tightening comparator and no second strict frontier.
technical_internal_limitation: The two slopes do not form a Markov state because clipped-UCB decisions also depend on the inverse ridge Gram coordinates. The open-ended question therefore concerns the slope projection of the augmented chain \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\) on \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}\); \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\) indexes only its initial slopes and is not an invariant chain state space. This bounded Rademacher recursion is not yet shown to have finite projected tail selection, a relative-basin-interior Cesaro attraction modulus, or any separately specified causal-score structure, so it is not claimed to belong to \(\mathfrak P_T\) and Theorems 1--2 are not claimed to apply. Optional Gaussian moment-extension subquestion: after the bounded-model dynamics are classified, determine whether the published Gaussian-noise recursion admits analogous dynamics under suitable moment controls. This optional subquestion is not a premise, deliverable, theorem, or part of the bounded-model open-ended question. Correct coverage at one isolated nominal level also does not identify the scale mixture: two unequal basin variances can be paired with a deterministic scale whose symmetric interval has the desired probability at that one level. Theorem 3 deliberately requires every nominal level.
honest_scope: The project establishes a field-tier inference frontier conditional on membership in the common-envelope finite-attractor class. Saco is the only direct strict-tightening comparator; the absence of a second direct strict frontier caps the contribution at field tier, which is the requested floor and achieved target. Guo--Xu, Shen and coauthors, Han, Leiner--Dunn--Ramdas, Borkar, and the remaining cited papers serve as informed-by comparators, ingredients, close motivation, or orthogonal regimes. The project treats a growing-horizon superpopulation adaptive experiment with a known randomization rule, not a pure fixed-finite-population randomization theorem. The bounded two-basin construction is solely an elementary, non-novel existence witness for strict logical separation between contrastwise and matrixwise invariance. It is not evidence that either the specified bounded Rademacher analogue or the published Gaussian no-intercept Guo--Xu recursion satisfies the finite-attractor, attraction, or common-envelope conditions. The open-ended question concerns only the slope-projected dynamics of the augmented bounded chain and does not assert membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) or applicability of Theorems 1--2. Any future inference theorem must separately specify its causal score, parameter space, unique target root, nonzero target contrast, induced scalar target, and every class assumption. The Gaussian moment extension remains optional and open. When \(m=1\), \(J=1\), \(V_J=V_1\) is deterministic, Theorem 1 is ordinary asymptotic normality, Theorem 2 is ordinary realized-QV studentization, and Theorems 3--4 allow \(\Sigma=V_1\).
